articles.rephrased_article: Espen Barth Eide, Norwegian Foreign Minister, urged India and Norway to increase their engagement to avoid becoming overly reliant on any single global power.  He highlighted the potential for increased trade, technology transfer, and renewable energy cooperation as key areas of focus. While Norway prefers India reduce its reliance on Russian oil, it acknowledges India's concerns regarding energy security.

articles.title: AI boom: Global stock market order shuffles as Taiwan, South Korea overtake Western giants - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The South Korean Kospi stock market has experienced a significant surge, more than tripling in less than 18 months, surpassing even the Nasdaq's bull run in the 1990s. This rally has propelled South Korea to eighth place globally in equity-market capitalisation rankings, overtaking the UK.  While analysts point to the sustainability of this rally compared to the dotcom bubble, concerns remain about the concentration of capital into a few AI firms, particularly TSMC and Samsung Electronics. The surge in Asian markets is also attracting foreign investment, with some analysts suggesting it may be driven by interest in AI and semiconductor themes.

articles.title: WHO says Ebola risk high regionally, low worldwide - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organisation (WHO) declared a public health emergency of international concern for the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, but not a pandemic.  Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief, stated that while investigations into the outbreak's origins are ongoing, it likely began two months ago and the scale of the situation in eastern DRC is much larger than confirmed cases. Lucille Blumberg, chair of the WHO emergency committee, said the current situation does not meet the criteria for a pandemic emergency.  Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, criticized the WHO's response to the outbreak as being "a little late".

articles.title: What’s the significance of the Russian president’s visit to China? | International Trade News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin visited China, meeting with Xi Jinping to strengthen ties between the two nations.  The visit comes a week after Donald Trump's trip to Beijing, highlighting the strength of their partnership. The leaders emphasized their shared opposition to US actions and policies, including the war against Iran and global tariffs. They discussed a potential multipolar world order where the United States does not hold dominance.

articles.title: Austrian ex-intelligence officer found guilty of Russia spying charges
articles.rephrased_article: Egisto Ott, a former Austrian intelligence officer, has been found guilty of spying for Russia and other charges. A jury in Vienna sentenced him to four years and one month in prison after finding him guilty of providing information to Russian intelligence officers and fugitive executive Jan Marsalek.  The case has raised concerns about the potential for continued Russian espionage activity within Austria. Prosecutors allege that Ott, who denies the charges, received payment from Marsalek for his actions. The investigation into Marsalek, also an Austrian citizen wanted by German authorities, is ongoing.

articles.title: Man charged with stealing camera equipment from Bondi shooting victim in aftermath of terror attack | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: NSW police have charged a 35-year-old man with larceny and disposing of stolen property in connection to the Bondi Beach terror attack. The man allegedly stole camera equipment from one of the victims, a retired police officer and photographer, after the December 14th shooting that killed 15 people. During an investigation into the attack, detectives identified the theft and executed a search warrant in Sydney's north-western suburbs where they found stolen property, including a camera, handcuffs, electronic devices, and white crystal powder. The man was granted strict conditional bail to appear before Blacktown local court on June 22nd.

articles.title: 'There won’t be escalation': Donald Trump reacts to Raúl Castro DOJ indictment over 1996 civilian plane shootdown - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump downplayed fears of escalating tensions with Cuba following the indictment of former president Raúl Castro for his role in the 1996 shooting down of civilian aircraft. Todd Blanche, acting Attorney General, announced the charges against Castro and five others, accusing him of conspiracy to kill US nationals and related offenses.  The incident, which saw two small planes destroyed by Cuban fighter jets, has long been a point of contention between the two countries. Díaz-Canel, the current Cuban president, has rejected accusations from the US while Trump maintains his focus on expanding influence in the Western Hemisphere.

articles.title: Modi, Shah are traitors who are attacking the Constitution, says Rahul at Rae Bareli meet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress party, criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, accusing them of attacking the Constitution and supporting industrialists. He also warned of an impending economic crisis, stating that it would disproportionately affect ordinary citizens while benefiting those in power.  Gandhi unveiled a statue of Veera Pasi in Rae Bareli, highlighting his party's renewed focus on the community. He further criticized the BJP government over land acquisition policies and unemployment rates, vowing to fight for the rights of the people.

articles.title: US stocks today: Dow soars 600 pts, Nasdaq 1.5% as chip stocks rally eyeing Nvidia results, Iran peace deal hopes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index rallied, boosted by optimism surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) despite concerns about the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and rising inflation. Nvidia, the leading AI chipmaker, is expected to release its report later today, which could influence investor sentiment.  While energy prices and inflation remain factors of uncertainty, investors are increasingly focusing on the potential of AI, driving gains in technology stocks like Astera Labs and ARM Holdings. The S&P 500 gained 1.08%, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.54%.

articles.title: Afridi, Aleema claim shots were fired at Adiala sit-in participants - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sohail Afridi, the Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Aleema Khan, Imran Khan's sister, held a press conference in Islamabad where they claimed shots were fired at participants of a sit-in protesting Imran Khan's imprisonment. They alleged that the government was blocking wheat supplies to the province and that the treatment of Imran's family was unfair.  They announced plans for further protests, including one on Friday. The Tehreek Tahaffuz Ayeen-e-Pakistan (TTAP) and the PTI also announced nationwide protests against Imran Khan's imprisonment.

articles.title: James Murdoch to acquire New York Magazine and Vox Media Podcast Network | Media News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: James Murdoch, the younger son of media mogul Rupert Murdoch, has acquired New York Magazine and the Vox Media Podcast Network in a deal valued at over $300 million.  The acquisition gives Murdoch control of a storied magazine known for its coverage of culture, politics, and fashion, as well as a podcast division with a reach comparable to cable television news networks. The deal also includes the Vox Media podcast network, which boasts popular programs like "Pivot," and will see Vox Media CEO Jim Bankoff join Lupa Systems, the company owned by Murdoch.

articles.title: US charges former Cuban president Raúl Castro over 1996 downing of planes
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has charged former Cuban leader Raúl Castro with conspiracy to kill US nationals and other crimes over the downing of two planes in 1996. The charges, revived from a 2003 case, accuse Castro and five others of shooting down an aircraft belonging to Brothers to the Rescue and killing four people, including three Americans. President Miguel Díaz-Canel of Cuba called the charges "a political manoeuvre, devoid of any legal foundation" while Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche stated that the US would also charge Castro with destruction of aircraft and murder counts.  The move comes amidst increased US pressure on Cuba's communist rule.

articles.title: Canada faces calls for investigation into death of woman after plasma donation | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Patient advocates are calling for a new investigation into the death of Rodiyat Alabede, a young woman who died after donating plasma in Winnipeg.  Health Canada initially found no link between her death and the donation, but campaigners allege significant discrepancies between the autopsy report and the agency's medical summary. Grifols, the company that operated the facility where Alabede donated, has acknowledged issues with staff training and reporting, but maintains it is working to address them.  The advocacy group representing Alabede's family is demanding a reopened investigation and the suspension of Grifols' license pending further review.

articles.title: RBI to infuse liquidity via $5 billion dollar rupee swap auction on May 26 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will hold a USD/INR buy/sell swap auction on May 26th to address the recent depreciation of the rupee. The central bank aims to stabilize the currency by selling dollars and boosting forex reserves, which have been depleted due to interventions in the foreign exchange market. This is the first such swap since February 28th, when geopolitical tensions began. Banks will sell dollars to the RBI at a predetermined premium, with successful bids accepted at their quoted rate.

articles.title: TACO abroad, boss at home: Trump may be losing against China or Iran, but still controls MAGA | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's foreign policy, particularly his handling of the Iran conflict, has led to a mixed bag of results. While he may be losing public support and facing congressional rebuke, he remains powerful within the Republican Party. Trump's tactics of intimidation have proven effective in silencing dissenters, as evidenced by the defeat of Rep. Thomas Massie, who lost his primary election after refusing to pledge unwavering loyalty. This strategy has also led to a decline in public approval ratings and fueled concerns about his ability to lead effectively.  Despite these challenges, Trump continues to hold significant sway within the Republican Party, demonstrating that loyalty trumps ideology and seniority in American politics.

articles.title: SC issues notices to accused in Rawalpindi honour killing case after jirga rejects woman’s marriage choice - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of Pakistan issued notices to the accused in an honor killing case involving a young woman from Rawalpindi who was murdered after a jirga rejected her choice of marriage. The case stems from an FIR filed by Zia-ur Rehman, alleging his wife's elopement with another man and subsequent murder at the behest of a jirga. Zafarullah and Rafaqat Mehmood, members of the jirga who were granted bail by the Lahore High Court, are among those facing charges. The Punjab Prosecution Department appealed against the high court's decision, arguing that the accused were fully involved in the crime and posed a threat to witnesses. The case was adjourned until June.

articles.title: Trump administration indicts Cuba’s Raul Castro over 1996 plane shootdown | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Justice Department indicted former Cuban President Raul Castro in connection with the 1996 downing of civilian planes operated by the Miami-based exile group Brothers to the Rescue. The indictment alleges that Castro, Cuba’s defense minister at the time, played a leading role in the decision to shoot down the aircraft.  Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche stated that the US will pursue accountability for those who kill Americans and that this case represents a major step toward justice for the families of four murdered Americans. The indictment has been met with strong reactions from Cuba’s current leader, Miguel Diaz-Canel, who accused the Trump administration of political maneuvering and lying about the events of 1996.

articles.title: What we know about the San Diego mosque attack suspects
articles.rephrased_article: San Diego Police Chief Scott Wahl and the Council on American-Islamic Relations-San Diego (Cair-SD) confirmed that five people, including the two teenage suspects, died in a shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego. The attack occurred on Monday afternoon, with authorities responding to reports of an active shooter.  The suspects were found dead from self-inflicted wounds in a vehicle near the mosque. Amin Abdullah, a security guard and father of eight, is being hailed as a hero for stopping the attack and saving lives. Authorities are investigating the incident as a possible hate crime, seizing over 30 guns and tactical gear from the suspects' residences.

articles.title: Russian jet causes ‘dangerous’ near miss after flying close to RAF spy plane | Royal Air Force | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Russian Su-27 and Su-35 jets flew within six meters of an RAF Rivet Joint spy plane in separate incidents over the Black Sea last month.  The incidents, described as "dangerous and unacceptable" by Defense Secretary John Healey, raised concerns about potential diplomatic crisis between the two countries. The MoD stated that these actions create a serious risk of accidents and escalation.

articles.title: Centre tells Supreme Court no new hydel projects should come up in upper Ganga - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union government has submitted to the Supreme Court that no new hydroelectric projects should be permitted in the upper reaches of the Ganga in Uttarakhand. The Ministries of Environment, Jal Shakti and Power presented a single affidavit stating this position, citing concerns about cumulative impact on the ecosystem and seismic fragility. This decision comes after years of expert recommendations and court orders regarding dam development's potential to exacerbate flooding risks.  The matter is scheduled for hearing on May 20th.

articles.title: Sebi proposes to permit third-party payment in mutual funds in certain scenarios - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, the Indian markets regulator, proposed allowing third-party payments in mutual funds for specific scenarios such as employer-sponsored investments and AMC payment of commissions. The proposals aim to balance ease of investing with investor protection by implementing safeguards like KYC checks and electronic fund trails. Sebi seeks public comments on these changes until June 10th.

articles.title: GHMC officials’ negligence will turn Hyderabad into concrete jungle: Justice Shravan Kumar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana High Court ordered the removal of illegal encroachments on public roads at Block no. 16, HIG-II in Hyderabad after finding that GHMC authorities had been derelict in their duty. The court instructed HYDRAA, a government organization responsible for urban development, to take immediate action to restore the area according to approved plans and ordered the government to hold erring officers accountable for their inaction.

articles.title: TGBCESDTC to conduct 4-day AI and life skills training programme - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana BC Employability Skill Development and Training Centre (TGBCESDTC), in collaboration with the Magic Bus India Foundation, will host a four-day interactive workshop from May 21 to June 11 across various districts of Telangana. The program aims to introduce district-level youth to artificial intelligence technologies and enhance their employability skills.  Interested youth are advised to contact their nearest TGBCESDTC centers for enrollment and further information.

articles.title: Hindu groups perform puja at Bhojshala amid security; ASI issues directions to implement High Court order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hindu Front for Justice, Bhoj Utsav Samiti, and local residents performed Aarti at the Bhojshala complex in Madhya Pradesh's Dhar on Saturday, May 16, 2026. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) acknowledged the High Court's verdict declaring the site a Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Saraswati and a Sanskrit learning center.  The ASI issued an order permitting unrestricted access for the Hindu community while ensuring monument conservation under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958. Muslim representatives have stated they will challenge the decision in the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Mayawati demands extensive relief for storm victims in Uttar Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mayawati, president of the Bahujan Samaj Party, called on the Uttar Pradesh government to provide extensive support to families affected by recent storms and heavy rain that have caused at least 111 deaths. She urged the government to help people rebuild their lives after the destruction of property and loss of life.

articles.title: Full list of Kerala Cabinet Ministers by May 17, says Satheesan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.D. Satheesan, the newly appointed Chief Minister of Kerala, indicated that the full list of Ministers will be presented to Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar by Sunday evening.  The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for Monday at 10 a.m., with speculation surrounding potential ministerial appointments within the United Democratic Front (UDF). Senior Congress leader Ramesh Chennithala, reportedly disgruntled over not being chosen as Chief Minister, is rumored to be joining the Cabinet as Home Minister.  K.C. Venugopal, an aspirant for the CM's post, also met with Mr. Chennithala in conciliatory talks. The UDF is expected to finalize its ministerial appointments after discussions with all partners.

articles.title: NCC annual training camp begins - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The NCC Group Training Centre, West Hill, hosted the annual training camp for 380 cadets from Kozhikode, Kannur, and Palakkad districts.  The ten-day program, led by Col. Venkatesan R., Commanding Officer of the NCC 9 Kerala Girls Battalion, aims to foster civic sense and social responsibility in participants through classes on personality development, health and hygiene, self-defense, and NCC subject training. The camp concludes on May 22nd.

articles.title: Bidadi township: Deve Gowda announces stir against project; DKS hits back - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: H.D. Deve Gowda, former Prime Minister, launched a campaign against the proposed Bidadi township project, claiming it targets fertile agricultural land and is driven by a "land business." He accused the Siddaramaiah government of facilitating this project under the guise of urban development, drawing parallels with previous satellite township projects that were withdrawn due to public opposition. D.K. Shivakumar, Deputy Chief Minister, countered Gowda's accusations, alleging that the Kumaraswamy family amassed wealth through real estate dealings and initiated similar projects in the past.

articles.title: Body donated for educational purposes cannot be returned: Kerala HC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala High Court ruled that a woman's body, donated to the Government Medical College, Kalamassery, cannot be returned based on her children's request. The court emphasized that the deceased's intention to donate her body for educational purposes overrides any subsequent requests from her children.  As a result, the court dismissed their plea seeking the return of their mother's remains.

articles.title: Average of 53% MPs attend meetings of 16 Parliamentary Standing Committees, PAC: data - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been raising concerns about the low attendance of members at parliamentary committees.  Data shows that an average of 53% of members attended meetings of 16 department-related Standing Committees and the Public Accounts Committee since their reconstitution last September, with five meetings postponed due to a lack of quorum. The data also reveals that nearly 47% of members were absent from these meetings, with better attendance observed in committees focused on Railways, Petroleum and Natural Gas, External Affairs, and Finance.  The Standing Committees discussed various important subjects including India-Sri Lanka relations, the review of the working of Border Roads Organisation (BRO), research and technology development in renewable energy, and safety and security of the diaspora during the ongoing conflict in West Asia.

articles.title: Athlete Swapna Barman becomes victim of poll violence, house attacked - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Swapna Barman, an Asian Games gold medalist and Trinamool Congress candidate, reported that her property was set on fire by unidentified individuals after the 2026 West Bengal Assembly election. Abhishek Banerjee, a Trinamool Congress general secretary, accused BJP supporters of the arson attack and claimed it reflects the "violence, intimidation, and fear" directed at Trinamool supporters.  The BJP government has denied these allegations while Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari pledged to ensure the safety of those displaced by violence.

articles.title: Iran warns of readiness for war and economic costs as US talks falter | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, warned that the US-led war on Iran is impacting American households through rising inflation and debt costs.  He also stated that a lack of trust with the United States has hindered negotiations.  Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, parliament speaker, mocked the US for funding a "failed TV host" to act as Secretary of War in the Persian Gulf. Ebrahim Azizi, head of Iran’s National Security Commission, announced plans to control traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and impose fees on vessels that do not cooperate with Iran.  The Iranian government has called on citizens to take to the streets for nightly demonstrations, while state-run media promotes a call to arms.

articles.title: Man arrested for murdering woman, dumping body in Tirupalya lake in Anekal taluk - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ratan Das, a man from Assam, was arrested in connection with the murder of a 47-year-old woman whose body was found floating in Tirupalya Lake in Anekal taluk.  Police confirmed that the woman had been strangled and suffocated before being disposed of in thick grass near the lake. The investigation revealed that Das had an illicit relationship with the victim and confessed to killing her after pressure to marry. He is currently under judicial custody.

articles.title: Tens of thousands turn out for UK far-right rally, counter protest - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Tens of thousands attended a rally organized by far-right activist Tommy Robinson in London, where he urged attendees to be "peaceful and courteous."  A counter-demonstration, combining with an anti-fascism march organized by the Stand Up to Racism group, drew smaller crowds. The Metropolitan Police deployed 4,000 officers for the event, citing concerns about potential clashes between rival groups and a heightened threat level due to recent violent attacks targeting London's Jewish community.  Elon Musk, owner of X (formerly Twitter), addressed Robinson's rally last September via video-link. Prime Minister Keir Starmer condemned the organizers of Robinson's rally, accusing them of "peddling hatred and division."

articles.title: Abu-Bilal al-Minuki: ISIL’s shadow commander in West Africa | ISIL/ISIS News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US and Nigeria jointly killed Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, a key ISIL figure, in a military operation in Borno state.  Al-Minuki was described as the second-in-command of ISIL (ISIS) and had been under US sanctions since 2023. The Nigerian army said he was responsible for providing guidance to ISIL entities outside Nigeria on media operations, economic warfare, and weapons manufacturing. Experts believe that while this operation is a tactical win, it will not be a decisive blow against ISWAP's overall capabilities due to the group's decentralized command structure.  The US and Nigeria are committed to continuing their fight against terrorism in the region.

articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Congress demands resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders demanded the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, the Union Education Minister, over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal.  They accused the government of a "money-making racket" involving people linked to the ruling establishment and claimed that the incident had caused immense trauma for 22 lakh students. Rahul Gandhi called for the Prime Minister's intervention, while Mallikarjun Kharge, the Congress president, alleged that the Modi government was undermining student credibility through repeated paper leaks.  Jairam Ramesh, a Congress general secretary, criticized the government's lack of action and incompetence in addressing exam reforms.

articles.title: Of roses and redlines: Trump faces thorny questions on Taiwan and trade
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump returned to the White House on Friday after a summit with Xi Jinping in Beijing, where he faced criticism for failing to secure concrete agreements and appearing hesitant to defend Taiwan militarily.  The trip, initially focused on trade and economic issues, shifted towards an intense negotiation over Taiwan, with Xi Jinping warning of potential repercussions if the US mishandled the "Taiwan question." Trump's reluctance to commit to a pending $14 billion weapons package for Taiwan and his failure to secure concessions on Iran or Hong Kong raised concerns about a shift in US policy toward China. Despite claiming major commercial victories, analysts remain skeptical about the actual benefits of the trip.

articles.title: Bannu police kill five militants after launching operation in district - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bannu Police have killed a highly wanted commander, Hiyatullah, and his accomplice during an operation targeting militants involved in the suicide attack on the Fateh Khel police post.  The police claim to have eliminated five terrorists within the last 24 hours following the attack which resulted in the deaths of at least 15 police personnel. The operations were conducted under the special directives of RPO Sajjad Khan and involved intelligence-based operations (IBOs) and specialized police teams. Civil society and local residents praised the Bannu Police for their commitment to maintaining law and order, while the Police Peace Committee launched an operation titled “Operation Revenge of the Martyrs” with a focus on reclaiming militant hideouts and holding individuals linked to them accountable.

articles.title: Hamas confirms killing of Qassam Brigades leader in Israeli attack | Hamas News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Hamas confirmed the death of Izz al-Din al-Haddad, head of the armed wing of the Palestinian group in Gaza, in an Israeli attack that killed seven people. Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz stated that al-Haddad was targeted as one of the architects of the October 7th attacks.  Hamas condemned the "treacherous and cowardly assassination" and called it a breach of the Gaza ceasefire agreement, while also reaffirming its resistance against Israel. The Palestinian Mujahideen Movement and its military wing, the Mujahideen Brigades, mourned al-Haddad's death.

articles.title: Colorado governor faces backlash over clemency for 2020 election denier Tina Peters
articles.rephrased_article: Governor Jared Polis of Colorado faced criticism from fellow Democrats and some Republicans after commuting the prison sentence of former county clerk Tina Peters, a 2020 election denier convicted of tampering with election equipment.  Secretary of State Jena Griswold called the decision "an affront to our democracy", while President Donald Trump praised Peters' release on social media. Peters expressed remorse for her actions, but Governor Polis defended his commutation by arguing that her sentence was disproportionate for a first-time offender.

articles.title: Israeli strikes kill six in southern Lebanon hours after extension of ceasefire | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israel carried out airstrikes in southern Lebanon, killing at least six people, including three paramedics working at a health center.  The strikes came hours after Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend a ceasefire for another 45 days. Hezbollah, the Lebanese militant group, denounced the talks while Israel has only partially observed the truce. In Gaza, Israel confirmed the death of Hamas military chief Izz al-Din al-Haddad, who was suspected of planning the October 2023 attack on southern Israel. The strikes in Lebanon triggered a fresh exodus of civilians and raised concerns about a possible return to full-scale war in the region.

articles.title: Medical Education Minister demands court-monitored probe into NEET paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil criticized the ongoing investigation into the NEET question paper leak, calling for a court-monitored probe. He expressed concerns that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)'s current investigation lacked transparency and confidence, suggesting powerful individuals were involved in orchestrating the scandal to manipulate MBBS seat sales.

articles.title: Republican Louisiana senator in tough primary after Trump backs opponent | US Senate | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: In Louisiana's upcoming primary elections, Donald Trump's endorsement of Julia Letlow to challenge incumbent Bill Cassidy has created a significant political battle.  Cassidy, who voted to impeach the former president and later supported Robert F Kennedy Jr.'s nomination for health secretary, faces an uphill battle against Letlow and John Fleming. The changes to Louisiana's primary system, designed to favor pro-Trump candidates, have heightened Cassidy's challenges. While a runoff election is scheduled for June, Cassidy's campaign aims to secure the top two spots on Saturday and position themselves for a strong showing in the subsequent round.

articles.title: Students get clarity on career choices at The Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling Fair in Mysuru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Students attending the Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling Fair-2026 at Vidya Vardhaka College of Engineering in Mysuru sought guidance on their future career paths.  Experts from various fields provided information and advice to over 500 students, many accompanied by their parents, helping them navigate available career options based on individual interests and aptitudes.

articles.title: Harlem Renaissance documentary finally gets global premiere 50 years after cameras rolled | Documentary films | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: William Greaves, a pioneering documentary filmmaker, died in 2014 but his son David and granddaughter Liani are now completing his unfinished film "Once Upon a Time in Harlem."  The documentary, originally shot in 1972, captures the voices of artists, writers, musicians, and organizers from the Harlem Renaissance. The film features conversations about race, language, legacy, and the global reverberations of anti-colonial struggle. David Greaves believes that the film is timely given the current debates surrounding Black history and identity in America.  The film will have its international premiere at Cannes' Directors' Fortnight.

articles.title: Mango Diversity Show at Sangareddy FRC inaugurated - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Nagi Reddy, former Commissioner of Telangana State Election Commission, inaugurated the diamond jubilee celebrations and a two-day 'Mango Diversity Show' at the Fruit Research Station (FRS) in Sangareddy. The event, organized by the Sri Konda Laxman Telangana State Horticultural University (SKLTGHU), featured over 300 mango varieties and demonstrations of agricultural advancements for farmers.  The concluding day will include a 'Mango Processed Products Competition'.

articles.title: North America’s largest commuter rail system shuts down as workers strike | New York | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Long Island Rail Road (LIRR), North America's largest commuter rail system, was shut down on Saturday after five unions representing about half its workforce went on strike.  Janno Lieber, the MTA chairman, stated that the agency cannot accept a deal that would increase fares for riders. The unions are demanding higher wages and healthcare premiums to keep up with inflation and rising living costs. Kathy Hochul, New York's governor, urged both the MTA and the unions to return to negotiations and find a solution.

articles.title: BJP protests State government’s decision to withdraw uniform rule in educational institutions - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BJP district unit members protested against the State government's decision to withdraw uniform regulations in educational institutions, arguing that it would disrupt discipline and academic atmosphere. The protesters, including former MP Umesh Jadhav and BJP leaders Baburao Chavan, Sudha Halkai, Chandrakant Patil, and Ashok Bagli, demanded intervention from the Governor to retain the policy. They claimed uniforms promote secular values and reduce socioeconomic disparities among students.

articles.title: Lauren Boebert suggests Trump withheld funds to Colorado over prosecution of election denier | Colorado | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Lauren Boebert praised the commutation of Tina Peters' sentence, crediting President Donald Trump for the outcome. She also suggested that Peters' release could encourage Trump to stop blocking funds for a clean drinking water project in Colorado.  Boebert previously criticized colleagues for not standing up against Trump's veto of the bill, which would have provided clean water to 50,000 people.

articles.title: Starmer government bans 11 ‘far-right agitators’ from entering UK ahead of Tommy Robinson rally
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government has banned entry to 11 foreign individuals deemed "far-right agitators" ahead of a rally in London organized by anti-Islam activist Tommy Robinson.  Prime Minister Keir Starmer stated the ban aimed to prevent hate and violence, while Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood defended the decision as necessary for public good. The Metropolitan Police are deploying over 4,000 officers for one of its busiest days in years, with measures including facial recognition cameras, drone surveillance, and armored vehicles.  Concerns about potential flashpoints arise from a separate pro-Palestinian march taking place simultaneously.

articles.title: Remove Bandi Sanjay from Union Cabinet, Kavitha tells Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kalvakuntla Kavitha, president of the Telangana Rakshana Sena, urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to remove Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar from his position until the investigation and trial in the POCSO case involving his son are complete.  Kavitha expressed concern over potential conflict of interest and a perception of political influence on the investigation, arguing that public trust in the justice system could be damaged by Mr. Kumar's continued presence in office.

articles.title: Trump returns from China with stability and a stalemate - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's visit to Beijing, while highlighting a return to the familiar economic and strategic standoff between the US and China, produced modest results.  Xi Jinping appeared to describe the change with a new framework for their relationship, "constructive strategic stability," as China benefited from a retreat from the Trump administration’s trade war approach. Despite some commercial deals, such as Boeing aircraft sales, neither side secured significant commitments on issues like China's industrial overcapacity or its military ambitions in the Indo-Pacific.  Analysts suggest that the summit's thin commercial results reflect the US and China's continued competition despite a fragile truce.

articles.title: Kash Patel faces scrutiny over snorkeling outing at USS Arizona memorial in Hawaii | Hawaii | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: FBI Director Kash Patel is facing scrutiny for a snorkeling excursion around the USS Arizona memorial in Hawaii last summer. The incident was reported by the Associated Press, which obtained government emails describing the outing as a "VIP snorkel."  The Navy confirmed that Patel swam near the tomb for 30 minutes and the FBI defended the trip, stating it was a historical tour honoring heroes who died at Pearl Harbor. However, some experts have questioned whether such excursions are appropriate given the site's significance. The incident comes amid scrutiny of Patel's recent travel arrangements which have blurred lines between personal leisure and official business.

articles.title: King Charles ‘shocked and saddened’ as soldier dies after falling from horse at Royal Windsor Horse Show
articles.rephrased_article: A member of the King Charles III’s ceremonial artillery unit died following a fall from a horse at the Royal Windsor Horse Show on Friday evening. The soldier, serving with the King’s Troop Royal Horse Artillery, collapsed after leaving the arena and despite receiving immediate medical attention, suffered fatal injuries.  Police are treating the death as “unexplained but not suspicious” while investigations are ongoing in coordination with the Ministry of Defence and event organizers at the Royal Windsor Horse Show.

articles.title: BMRCL to electrify rails in underground section between Langford Town and Pottery Town - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) has issued a public warning regarding unauthorized access to the Reach-6 underground corridor. The electrification process, which will energize 33kV cables and the 750V DC third rail, is scheduled to begin on May 18th.  The BMRCL advises citizens against entering any underground metro section without authorization due to the risk of electrocution. The corporation emphasizes that it will not be held responsible for any injuries or casualties resulting from unauthorized access.

articles.title: Israeli army kills Palestinian man, raids homes in occupied West Bank | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli forces killed a 34-year-old Palestinian man in Jenin Camp, the Palestinian Ministry of Health confirmed. The army claims the victim was attempting to infiltrate the area where troops were operating.  The incident follows a series of raids on homes and settlements across the occupied West Bank, including attacks by Israeli settlers that resulted in arson and racist graffiti. UNRWA reports that these operations have displaced 40,000 Palestinians since last year. A UN official condemned the attacks against religious sites and civilian property and called for an investigation into the perpetrators.

articles.title: Litton's rearguard ton propels Bangladesh to 278 in Pakistan Test - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Litton Das scored a century to rescue Bangladesh from a top-order collapse in their second innings of the second Test against Pakistan, posting 278.  Pakistan reached 21-0 at stumps in reply with Azan Awais and Abdullah Fazal on 13 and 8 respectively.  The hosts lost six wickets for 49 runs after lunch, but Litton Das's century helped them reach a respectable total.

articles.title: Wes Streeting confirms he will stand if Labour leadership race is triggered | Wes Streeting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wes Streeting confirmed his intention to run for the Labour Party leadership if a contest is triggered, calling for a "proper contest" where candidates can showcase their ideas. He criticized Keir Starmer's leadership style and policies, including the winter fuel cut, arguing that Labour has lacked clarity of vision and direction since entering government.  Streeting also expressed his desire to rejoin the European Union, believing it would benefit the economy and strengthen national defense.

articles.title: Snorkeling at Pearl Harbor, Philadelphia concert date with girlfriend at $50,000 suite: Kash Patel unfazed by new controversies
articles.rephrased_article: FBI Director Kash Patel defended his recent trips, which included a snorkeling visit to the USS Arizona memorial in Hawaii. Patel was accompanied by nine others on the tour and was told not to touch the sunken ship. The FBI stated that the trip was part of official travel engagements with foreign counterparts.  The agency also confirmed Patel's attendance at a country music concert in Philadelphia with his girlfriend, Alexis Wilkins, who was an invited guest.

articles.title: Farmers worried as over 150 lorries loaded with paddy wait amid rain in Nagapattinam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 150 lorries carrying paddy procured through Direct Procurement Centres (DPCs) in Nagapattinam district have been stranded for over a week along the Puthur–Nagore East Coast Road due to delays in transportation and storage.  The accumulated stock, which includes samba and thaladi paddy, has raised concerns among farmers about potential damage from moisture exposure. The Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation (TNCSC) is working to clear the backlog but officials are confident it will be resolved within a day or two.

articles.title: How Thomas Massie came to represent Republican dissent in age of Trump | Government News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Congressman Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican known for his dissenting views on foreign policy and military aid to Israel, is facing a tough re-election bid against Ed Gallrein.  Massie has consistently voted against policies favored by the Trump administration, including tax bills and military interventions abroad. He has also been vocal in opposing unconditional US military aid to Israel. Pro-Israel groups have poured money into Gallrein's campaign, while Massie argues that this spending is a reflection of a foreign lobby attempting to influence elections. The outcome of the race could signal broader fault lines within the Republican base regarding foreign policy and support for Israel.

articles.title: Law Minister Tarar sees ‘no indication’ of 28th amendment for now - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar stated that the 28th Constitutional Amendment would require consultation with coalition partners and consensus on all issues. He clarified that constitutional amendments cannot be implemented without this process, noting ongoing discussions about population control, Hazara and Saraiki provinces, and local government systems.  PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari stated that the PPP has not been contacted by the government regarding a constitutional amendment and emphasized their role in previous amendments expanding provincial representation.

articles.title: At least eight people killed in Bangkok rail crossing collision | Thailand | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: At least eight people were killed and 32 injured in a train collision with a bus at a rail crossing in Bangkok, Thailand. Rescue officials and the deputy transport minister said the bus had stopped on the tracks at a red light, preventing crossing barriers from closing.  The train, carrying containers, was unable to stop in time, causing the collision. The incident also involved cars and motorcycles, with videos showing the train striking the bus and dragging vehicles along the tracks. Firefighters battled a blaze that engulfed the bus and nearby vehicles.

articles.title: At least eight dead, 25 injured in train collision that sparks bus fire in Thailand - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A freight train and a bus collided in Bangkok, Thailand on Saturday, killing at least eight people and injuring over 30. Bangkok police chief Urumporn Koondejsumrit confirmed the death toll and injuries, while Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul ordered an investigation into the incident. The collision occurred at a busy downtown intersection, with witnesses describing the bus instantly bursting into flames after being struck by the train. Deadly transport accidents are common in Thailand due to factors such as speeding, drunk driving, and weak law enforcement.

articles.title: ‘Research here is world class’: son of Steve Jobs looks to invest in UK cancer care | Venture capital | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Reed Jobs, a venture capitalist and the son of Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, is leading an oncology-focused venture capital fund called Yosemite, which has invested in over 20 healthcare startups.  The firm focuses on gene therapy, cancer vaccines, radiopharmaceuticals, and artificial intelligence, with a goal of making cancer treatable and non-lethal. Yosemite receives funding from organizations like LifeArc, a UK-based not-for-profit focused on rare diseases, and has partnerships with universities like Oxford and Cambridge.  Jobs hopes to see a shift in cancer care towards early diagnosis and personalized treatment similar to advances made with HIV and cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Maldives scuba tragedy: Diver dies in search of five Italian tourists who drowned in underwater cave
articles.rephrased_article: Sergeant Major Mohamed Mahudhee, one of eight divers searching for the bodies of five Italian scuba divers who died in a cave dive, has also passed away during the recovery operations. The Maldivian military expressed condolences to his family and colleagues. The cause of the divers' deaths is still under investigation, but experts suspect oxygen toxicity or panic as possible factors.

articles.title: A reality check on govt.’s claim of 45 days of LPG ‘rolling stock’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's government claims to have 45 days of LPG in stock, but experts question this figure given the country's limited storage capacity and reliance on imports.  The government has ordered several ships carrying LPG to arrive in India, with some already en route. The arrival of these tankers will contribute to the overall supply, although a significant shortfall remains.

articles.title: Police Peace Committee in Bannu launches operation against militants - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Police Peace Committee in Bannu launched an operation titled “Operation Revenge of the Martyrs” following a meeting where committee members discussed security measures and public cooperation. The committee president, Hazrat Ullah, emphasized continued operations against militants and vowed to avenge the deaths of police martyrs.  The committee also announced plans to reclaim militant-controlled properties and address individuals suspected of supporting them.

articles.title: LIVE: Chelsea vs Manchester City – FA Cup final | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Manchester City dominated possession in the early stages of the FA Cup final against Chelsea, with several chances created by Haaland and Rodri.  Chelsea struggled to create any meaningful attacks, but a strong defensive effort from Khusanov prevented Joao Pedro from scoring. The match remained scoreless at halftime.

articles.title: Mick Jagger and Eric Clapton win battle to stop 29-storey block being built by Thames | Planning policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mick Jagger, Eric Clapton, Felicity Kendal, and Harry Hill successfully opposed a 29-storey tower proposed by Rockwell Property on the banks of the River Thames. The developer's plans, initially for a 34-storey building with 142 flats, were rejected by Wandsworth council and the Greater London Authority due to concerns about its height, scale, and impact on the local area's character. A planning inspector agreed with these objections, concluding that the tower would be "overbearing" and "harmful."  The developer expressed disappointment over the decision but stated they had made changes to the scheme based on public feedback.

articles.title: New USCIS signature rule for H-1B, Green Card: Dos and don'ts for your next immigration application
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Homeland Security has issued an interim rule that expands the authority to reject immigration benefit requests due to signature issues. The rule, effective July 10, 2026, clarifies acceptable signature formats and outlines what constitutes a deficient signature.  Immigration experts warn that even minor signature errors can lead to case delays and potential loss of filing fees. This new rule applies to all individuals seeking immigration benefits under the US framework.

articles.title: Push for public transport exposes structural gaps - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's push for public transport, particularly metro rail, has prompted politicians and bureaucrats to use such systems. However, the renewed spotlight on public transit highlights a gap between policy intent and on-ground delivery.  Years of underinvestment in mass rapid transit systems have led to stalled projects like the Hyderabad Metro’s second phase and the Multi-Modal Transport System (MMTS) network. While efforts are underway to improve connectivity and funding, challenges remain, including securing approvals for expansion and procuring new train sets. The State government is also exploring a Rapid Rail Transit System (RRTS), but its suitability for urban settings remains questioned.

articles.title: UK police brace for far-right rally and counter-demonstration - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of people gathered in London for two opposing demonstrations: a far-right rally organized by Tommy Robinson and a counter-demonstration combining pro-Palestinian and anti-fascist sentiments. The Metropolitan Police deployed 4,000 officers to manage the events, citing concerns about potential violence and clashes between rival groups.  The Met has imposed strict conditions on both rallies, including restrictions on routes and timings, in an effort to keep attendees separated. Elon Musk, owner of X (formerly Twitter), addressed a similar rally organized by Robinson last year, drawing large crowds and sparking controversy.

articles.title: Zimbabwe’s diaspora reshapes real estate and farming investment trends | Features | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Zimbabwean digital influencers, Kundai Chitima and Kelvin Birioti, are influencing diaspora investment decisions through their social media content.  Their videos highlight opportunities in real estate, farming, and market trends, prompting some diaspora members to reconsider returning or investing in Zimbabwe. Nyashadzashe Nguwo, an Africa market entry advisor based in the UK, states that many individuals are relocating due to a combination of emotional and lifestyle-driven factors, including a desire to reconnect with their roots and contribute to national development.  Catherine Mutisi, a diaspora member who had previously invested in Zimbabwe, credits social media content for shifting her perspective on returning permanently. Economic pressures, such as high unemployment rates and rising living costs, continue to influence migration decisions, but the strong economic link between Zimbabwe and its diaspora remains significant, with diaspora investment playing a crucial role in various sectors.

articles.title: Toddlers among more than 50 schoolchildren kidnapped in Nigeria
articles.rephrased_article: Over 50 children, mostly toddlers aged two to five, were kidnapped from three schools in Mussa, Borno state, Nigeria. Gunmen used the children as human shields while fleeing on motorbikes, preventing security forces from responding. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, and government officials have not responded to requests for comment. The incident has prompted residents to flee the area, leaving traumatized parents waiting anxiously for news about their children.

articles.title: Soldier dies after falling from horse at Royal Windsor Horse Show | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A soldier from the King’s Troop, Royal Horse Artillery died after falling from their horse at the Royal Windsor Horse Show on Friday evening.  The incident occurred after a display and despite receiving immediate medical treatment, the soldier was pronounced dead at the scene. Police are investigating the cause of death but consider it to be unexplained. The show is continuing as planned with the omission of the King’s Troop’s display.

articles.title: Israel says Hamas military chief, involved in planning October 7 attacks, killed in Gaza
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli forces targeted and killed Izz al-Din al-Haddad, the head of Hamas' military wing, in a Gaza City airstrike.  The IDF stated that Haddad assumed leadership after the death of Mohammed Sinwar and was involved in planning attacks against Israeli civilians and troops. The IDF also claimed to have killed two other Hamas operatives, Hamer Iyad Muhammad Almatouk and Khaled Muhammad Salem Joudeh, who were accused of infiltrating Israel during the October 7th attacks.  Haddad's death follows a series of airstrikes targeting Hamas leaders in Gaza, as both sides continue to accuse each other of ceasefire violations.

articles.title: Kamal meets Vijay, submits 6 demands Tamil film industry’s development - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kamal Haasan, founder of Makkal Needhi Maiam, met with Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to discuss the development of the Tamil film industry.  Haasan presented six demands, including eliminating manual scavenging through technology and establishing village libraries and skill development centers. He also requested the abolition of local body entertain taxes on movie tickets, a strong anti-piracy team, and a state-owned OTT platform for Tamil cinema.

articles.title: Alleged drug queenpin Anmol remanded into police custody till May 22 in narcotics case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A judicial magistrate in Karachi remanded alleged drug queenpin Anmol alias Pinky into police custody until May 22nd.  She was arrested earlier this week for possession of narcotics and an unlicensed weapon, and is already facing multiple criminal charges. The police sought her physical custody in a total of 15 cases but were denied in most instances, with some being sent to judicial remand. Anmol claimed she was tortured during custody and that the police are trying to harass her in court.  The investigation into her alleged drug network is ongoing.

articles.title: Tens of thousands march in London in far-right and pro-Palestine protests | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tens of thousands of people marched in central London for two separate protests on Saturday: a pro-Palestine demonstration and a far-right rally organized by Tommy Robinson.  The Metropolitan Police deployed 4,000 officers, including reinforcements from outside the city, to manage the events. The police warned that they would adopt a "zero-tolerance approach" to hate crime and said organizers would be legally responsible for ensuring invited speakers do not break hate speech laws. Prime Minister Keir Starmer condemned the far-right rally as peddling hatred and division.

articles.title: Rescue diver dies during search for bodies of Italians who drowned in Maldives caves
articles.rephrased_article: Rescue diver Staff Sgt Mohamed Mahdhee died while searching for the bodies of four Italians who drowned in Maldivian caves. The five divers, part of a University of Genoa team and a boat operations manager/diving instructor, were exploring a depth of around 60m when they disappeared on Thursday. Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu visited the area to observe the search efforts.  The incident is believed to be the worst single diving accident in the nation's history. The other divers have been accounted for and are receiving assistance from the Italian Embassy in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

articles.title: Two men arrested in London after man run over by van in Birmingham | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Two men were arrested in London after arriving for a protest in the capital. The arrests are related to an incident in Birmingham where a man was run over by a van on Thursday evening. West Midlands police are investigating the incident, which left a man in his 30s with a broken leg that required surgery.  The van involved in the incident has been recovered and is being examined.

articles.title: Israel’s Image Crisis: Becoming Too Big to Spin? | TV Shows | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel is intensifying its public relations efforts to counter criticism of its actions in Gaza, Lebanon, Iran, and the West Bank. The push includes a major expansion of Hasbara, digital campaigns, and media messaging aimed at reversing declining support for Israel, particularly in the US.  However, critics argue that these efforts cannot erase the reality of ongoing violence and human rights concerns.

articles.title: 'He couldn’t stop blushing': When Queen Elizabeth II smiled at Prince Harry, his reaction said everything
articles.rephrased_article: A photograph of Queen Elizabeth II smiling at Prince Harry during his military training graduation in 2006 has resurfaced, capturing the warmth of their relationship.  Royal enthusiasts have praised the image for its genuine connection between the Queen and her grandson. The photo is a reminder of the Queen's supportive nature towards her grandchildren, including encouraging them to serve the public. Prince Harry served ten years in the British Army, including two tours to Afghanistan, and founded the Invictus Games to support injured veterans.

articles.title: CJI Surya Kant clarifies ‘parasites’ remarks, says youth are pillars of country - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant issued a statement clarifying that his remarks about "attacks" on institutions were not directed at the youth but at individuals with fake or bogus degrees in professions like law and media. He stated that these individuals act as parasites by attacking institutions without any legitimate standing. The CJI maintained that he holds immense respect for India's youth and expressed pride in their potential to contribute to a developed nation.

articles.title: Andalucíans to vote in election seen as gauge of Spain’s wider political change | Spain | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming election in Andalucía, Spain's most populous region, is expected to deliver an absolute majority for the conservative People’s Party (PP) and further weaken the Socialists. Juan Manuel Moreno Bonilla, the PP regional president, seeks to capitalize on scandals surrounding Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and his administration.  The PP aims to portray the election as a referendum on Sánchez's leadership, while Vox is expected to gain seats. The outcome will have implications for Spain's upcoming general election next year.

articles.title: Robert Lewandowski to leave Barcelona with his ‘mission complete’ | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Robert Lewandowski announced his departure from Barcelona at the end of his contract this summer. The veteran Polish striker, who joined from Bayern Munich in 2022, helped the club to three La Liga titles, including this season's trophy, and the Copa del Rey in 2025.  He expressed gratitude for the support he received from fans and described leaving with a sense of mission accomplished. Lewandowski will play his final game at Camp Nou on Sunday against Real Betis.

articles.title: The surprising reason Joan Kroc’s record-breaking Salvation Army gift still changes lives today
articles.rephrased_article: Joan Kroc's massive donation to the Salvation Army, totaling several billion dollars, resulted in the construction of a network of community centers known as Kroc Centers across the United States.  These centers provide a wide range of services including swimming instruction, fitness classes, youth sports activities, and educational programs, fostering social interaction and community engagement. The donation transformed the Salvation Army's strategy for community engagement by enabling the construction of sustainable facilities that could operate independently from traditional charity events. This tangible legacy has had a lasting impact on communities nationwide.

articles.title: BRICS is evolving with new members; differences will take time to resolve: Brazil FM Mauro Vieira - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The BRICS Foreign Ministers meeting in Delhi concluded with a detailed Chair Statement supporting Indian initiatives and the Palestinian cause, but failed to reach consensus on positions regarding the war in West Asia.  Despite disagreements, Mauro Vieira, Brazilian Foreign Minister, emphasized the continued importance of BRICS.

articles.title: Divers in Maldives resume search for Italian scuba divers who drowned in cave | Maldives | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Divers in the Maldives resumed their search for the bodies of four Italian scuba divers who drowned while exploring a deep underwater cave on Friday. The Maldives presidential spokesperson, Mohamed Hussain Shareef, said eight divers took part in the operation, working in pairs, with plans to continue the mission on Saturday.  The five Italians died in the accident in Vaavu Atoll on Thursday, and their bodies were recovered except for the remaining four divers who are believed to be inside the same cave. The Italian foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, said the Italian government will do everything possible to recover the bodies of the deceased.

articles.title: Amid the fertiliser crisis, Africa has a chemical-free option: Agroecology | Agriculture | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Amidst a looming global food crisis exacerbated by the US-Israel war on Iran, African states are urged to invest in sustainable agriculture through agroecology.  International agencies are concerned about the implications for Africa, where hundreds of millions face food shortages and many countries rely heavily on food imports. The reliance on chemical fertilizers has led to high costs, debt burdens, and environmental damage.  Experts propose shifting subsidies and policy initiatives towards supporting agroecological methods that increase food production, strengthen farmer livelihoods, and provide ecosystem benefits while reducing dependence on fossil fuel-based fertilizers.

articles.title: Why Robert F. Smith’s Morehouse surprise donation mattered even more after graduation day
articles.rephrased_article: Robert F. Smith, an entrepreneur, made a significant donation of $34 million to Morehouse College in 2019, covering the student debt for the graduating class and that of their parents. The gesture resonated widely due to its impact on both students' immediate financial burdens and the broader issue of educational debt in African-American communities.  This event highlighted the significant role family debt plays in college expenses and sparked a conversation about educational equality and financial empowerment within historically black colleges and universities (HBCUs).

articles.title: KTR asks party leaders and BLAs to be alert during SIR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.T. Rama Rao, working president of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), met with Assembly Constituency in-charges to discuss electoral roll revisions and membership drives. He cautioned against potential voter suppression by Congress and BJP.  He urged party members to protect voters' rights and expose the opposing parties' policies. At a separate meeting with Sanathnagar constituency activists, KTR stated that the BJP has minimal presence in the state and their Lok Sabha election performance was an anomaly.

articles.title: Peacock ‘invasion’ of Italian seaside town ruffles feathers | Italy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Federico Bruni, a resident of Punta Marina, Italy, finds the town's peacock population to be a charming addition.  However, some residents like Francesco and Marco are unhappy with the birds' presence due to their droppings and mating calls disrupting the peace. The peacocks have become increasingly numerous in recent years, likely due to supplementary feeding by locals during the Covid-19 pandemic.  The Ravenna city council is struggling to manage the situation, attempting to find a balance between respecting the birds' natural behavior and maintaining public order.

articles.title: Hamas confirms killing of military chief after Israeli strike - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Hamas’s armed wing chief, Ezzedine Al-Haddad, was killed in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza on Friday. The Israeli military and its intelligence agency, the Shin Bet, confirmed his death, stating he directed the planning of the October 7th massacre.  The Israeli military also claimed this is a significant operational achievement, following previous assassinations of Hamas leaders like Yahya Sinwar and Mohammed Deif. The conflict in Gaza continues with over 72,700 civilian deaths attributed to Israeli strikes since the ceasefire began in October.

articles.title: Ultra-Orthodox conscription dispute pushes Israeli government to brink | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Israeli government is facing a crisis due to the withdrawal of support from ultra-Orthodox parties, who are demanding an exemption from military conscription. The coalition has called for an early election following continued fractures over the issue.  Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government is struggling to address the demands of the ultra-Orthodox parties, with their spiritual leader calling for the dissolution of the Knesset. This situation has prompted calls for sanctions on those who refuse conscription and a potential end to benefits for religious students whose families rely on them. The Israeli military argues that recruiting ultra-Orthodox men is crucial for sustaining its operations in the region.

articles.title: Video: 8 killed, over 20 injured as freight train crashes into bus in Bangkok
articles.rephrased_article: At least eight people were killed and over 20 injured in a freight train collision with a public bus at a railway crossing in Bangkok, Thailand. Siripong Angkasakulkiat, Thailand's deputy transport minister, confirmed the deaths and said all bodies recovered were found inside the bus. The accident occurred near an airport rail link station late Saturday afternoon, with videos showing vehicles halted at the crossing before the collision.  Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.

articles.title: T.N. Cabinet portfolios: CM Vijay to hold Home; Finance for Sengottaiyan; Aadhav Arjuna gets PWD - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, has announced the portfolios for his cabinet members. Vijay will oversee key departments including Home, Police, and IAS/IPS officers.  N. Anand, the deputy chief minister, will handle Rural Development and Water Resources. Other ministers have been assigned specific responsibilities in areas such as health, education, finance, and energy. The Governor has approved the recommendations.

articles.title: Freight train and bus crash kills at least eight in Bangkok
articles.rephrased_article: An accident involving a freight train and a public bus in Bangkok has resulted in the deaths of at least eight people and injuries to 25 others. The collision, which triggered a fire that engulfed the bus, prompted emergency services to respond with firefighters and rescue crews.  The fire has been contained, but teams continue to search for victims and investigate the cause of the accident.

articles.title: Arrest of Iraqi terror suspect with alleged links to Iran’s Quds Force is astonishing but not surprising | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: An alleged Iraqi commander of an Iranian-backed militia group, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, has been arrested in the US on charges of orchestrating 18 terrorist attacks across Europe and Canada since the beginning of the Iran war. The complaint alleges that al-Saadi is responsible for a string of recent firebombings, an arson attack on a synagogue, and a shooting at the US consulate in Toronto, as well as a wave of attacks on Jewish targets in the UK.  Al-Saadi allegedly posted claims of responsibility for attacks on social media platforms under the name of Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia (HAYI), a group believed to be linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The arrest comes as no surprise to investigators and analysts who have long suspected Iranian involvement in these attacks.

articles.title: SIR in Telangana: Draft electoral rolls to have names of electors whose Enumeration Forms are received - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Electoral Registration Officers (ERO) in Telangana will publish draft electoral rolls on July 31, 2026, including names of all electors whose Enumeration Forms were received.  Following this, EROs will issue notices to individuals who cannot be linked or have discrepancies in their linking with the previous revision's electoral rolls. This is part of a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) conducted for the first time since 2002 when Telangana was part of united Andhra Pradesh.

articles.title: Wembanyama’s Spurs reach Western finals, Pistons stay alive in NBA playoffs | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The San Antonio Spurs advanced to the Western Conference Finals with a 139-109 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves, while the Detroit Pistons defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 115-94 to level their Eastern Conference semifinal series at 3-3.  Victor Wembanyama, who was ejected from game four for an elbow incident with Naz Reid, led the Spurs with 21 points and 19 rebounds. The Pistons, led by Cade Cunningham's 21 points, will face a decisive Game Seven in Detroit to advance to the next round.

articles.title: Bhojshala Case: What did the High Court decide? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madhya Pradesh High Court ruled that the Bhojshala-Kamal Maula site is a Hindu temple, granting full worship rights. The verdict has sparked reactions from both sides and may now be appealed to the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Trump says ISIL second-in-command Abu-Bilal al-Minuki killed | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced that Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, the second-in-command of ISIL (ISIS), was killed in a joint operation by US and Nigerian forces.  The operation, which involved a meticulously planned mission, eliminated the "most active terrorist in the world" according to Trump. The US State Department designated al-Minuki as a global terrorist in 2023 for his links to ISIL, highlighting his role as a Sahel-based ISIL senior leader and part of its General Directorate of Provinces.

articles.title: Cyberabad police begin search for Bandi Bageerath in Hyderabad and Karimnagar after HC rejects pre-arrest bail plea - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cyberabad police intensified their search for Bandi Bageerath, accused of sexually assaulting and emotionally manipulating a 17-year-old girl, by conducting searches at his residences in Hyderabad and Karimnagar.  Five police teams were involved in the operation, which included physical checks and surveillance efforts to track his whereabouts. The investigation is ongoing, with discussions about Bageerath surrendering to authorities before being subjected to medical examination and remanded.

articles.title: US charges alleged Iran-backed ⁠Kataib Hezbollah suspect – What we know | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of Justice has arrested and charged an Iraqi national, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, with involvement in at least 18 attacks and attempted attacks spanning the US, Canada, and Europe. The charges against al-Saadi, a senior commander of the Iran-backed armed group Kataib Hezbollah, include conspiracy to provide material support to foreign terrorist organizations, conspiracy to provide material support for acts of terrorism, and provision of material support for acts of terrorism.  Al-Saadi is accused of coordinating international retaliation following the US, Israel, and Iran's military conflict in late February 2026. He appeared in a Manhattan federal court on Friday where he was hit with a six-count criminal complaint. Al-Saadi smiled throughout the hearing but did not speak and will remain jailed for the time being.

articles.title: Submerged temple emerges as Bhavanisagar Dam level drops - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bhavanisagar Dam's water level dropping to 59 ft. has revealed the dilapidated Sri Madhava Perumal Temple, which was submerged during construction in the 1940s and 1950s.  A study of inscriptions on the temple premises found it to be located at the confluence of the Bhavani and Moyar rivers, once a significant trade route connecting Kongu with Karnataka and Kerala. The site is believed to have been ruled by the Hoysalas and served as the location for a fort built by Madhava Perumal Dhandanayaka, a general appointed by King Veera Ballala III.  The temple was last visible in 2024 when the water level dropped, and fishermen report that portions of the structure become visible again at lower water levels.

articles.title: Gunmen kidnap dozens of students in Nigeria’s Borno State | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gunmen stormed a school in Borno State, Nigeria, kidnapping dozens of students. The attack, which bore the hallmark of the Boko Haram group, occurred at Mussa Primary and Junior Secondary School while classes were in session.  Local lawmaker Midala Usman Balami called the attack "heartbreaking" and urged authorities to act swiftly. This incident follows a string of similar kidnappings across Nigeria, highlighting the ongoing security challenges in the country's northeast. The community of Mussa lies near the Sambisa Forest, a longstanding stronghold of rebel fighters who have waged a campaign of violence in northeast Nigeria for over a decade.

articles.title: Manoj Jarange warns of fresh agitation over Maratha quota issue from May 30 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Manoj Jarange, a Maratha quota activist, announced an indefinite hunger strike beginning May 30th over the Maharashtra government's failure to distribute Kunbi caste certificates and implement other demands.  Jarange demanded the dissolution of the Maratha quota sub-committee and urged for a separate ministry for the Maratha and Kunbi communities. He also criticized the state government for halting the issuance of Kunbi caste certificates, claiming that officials have been instructed not to issue them. Devendra Fadnavis, the Chief Minister of Maharashtra, has been accused by Jarange of being responsible for these actions.

articles.title: Iran war day 78: Trump, Tehran signal talks as Lebanon truce extended | Border Disputes News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that the US administration has signaled openness to new negotiations aimed at ending the war.  He also said Tehran received communication from Trump's administration indicating willingness to continue talks, and that he was open to any support – including from China. Meanwhile, Lebanon extended a ceasefire with Israel for 45 days despite renewed violence. The truce extension was facilitated by US mediation after talks in Washington.  At least 12 people were killed on Friday, including three paramedics, according to Lebanese authorities.

articles.title: PM Modi arrives in Netherlands on second leg of five-nation tour - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in the Netherlands on Friday, May 15, 2026, for a two-day visit to further strengthen bilateral cooperation. Modi met with Dutch counterpart Rob Jetten, and will also meet with King Willem-Alexander and Queen Maxima. The visit is part of a five-nation tour that includes stops in Sweden, Norway, and Italy.  The trip comes as the India-EU Free Trade Agreement has been finalized, and the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement was signed in 2025.

articles.title: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon continue despite ‘ceasefire’ extension | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Despite a 45-day ceasefire extension agreed upon in Washington, Israel continued to bomb southern Lebanon on Saturday.  The Israeli army issued forced displacement orders for nine villages near Sidon and Nabatieh, while air strikes targeted at least five villages in the south.  Hezbollah opposes these negotiations and continues to oppose Israeli occupation of parts of Lebanon since the ceasefire took effect. The Lebanese presidency welcomed the extension but expressed concern over continued Israeli attacks.

articles.title: Rising diesel costs from Iran war strain US school budgets - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: US school districts are struggling to afford fuel costs due to soaring diesel prices since the start of the Iran war.  The price increase has forced many districts to tap emergency funds, consolidate routes, and reduce other programs. The situation is particularly challenging for districts in remote areas like Alaska and those with tight budgets, such as Yakima, Washington, where officials are facing a $213,000 annual fuel cost burden.  Some districts have found ways to mitigate the impact through alternative fuels or outsourcing transportation services, while others are grappling with the pressure of rising costs and potential service cuts.

articles.title: CBI arrests ‘mastermind’ linked to NEET-UG 2026 biology paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested a biology lecturer, Manisha Gurunath Mandhare, for her involvement in the 2026 NEET-UG paper leak case.  Mandhare, appointed by the National Testing Agency (NTA) as an expert, allegedly disclosed questions and answers from botany and zoology subjects to students through special coaching classes at her residence.
